title.local: St. Martin, Bishop of Tours, Confessor

parts.title: De Epístola prima beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Timótheum

verses.text: Fidélis sermo: si quis episcopátum desíderat, bonum opus desíderat.
Opórtet ergo epíscopum irreprehensíbilem esse, uníus uxóris virum, sóbrium, prudéntem, ornátum, pudícum, hospitálem, doctórem,
Non vinoléntum, non percussórem, sed modéstum; non litigiósum, non cúpidum, sed
Suæ dómui bene præpósitum, fílios habéntem súbditos cum omni castitáte.

responsory.text: Hic est Martínus, eléctus Dei Póntifex, cui Dóminus post Apóstolos tantam grátiam conférre dignátus est,
responsory.repeat: Ut in virtúte Trinitátis Deíficæ mererétur fíeri trium mortuórum suscitátor magníficus.

responsory.text: Sanctæ Trinitátis fidem Martínus conféssus est.
Ut in virtúte Trinitátis Deíficæ mererétur fíeri trium mortuórum suscitátor magníficus.

parts.title: Lesson from the first letter of St. Paul the Apostle to Timothy

verses.text: A faithful saying: if a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.
It behoveth therefore a bishop to be blameless, the husband of one wife, sober, prudent, of good behaviour, chaste, given to hospitality, a teacher,
Not given to wine, no striker, but modest, not quarrelsome, not covetous, but
One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all chastity.

responsory.text: This is that Martin whom God chose to be an High Priest unto Himself, he upon whom the Lord was pleased to bestow favour like as upon His Apostles;
responsory.repeat: So that he prevailed gloriously in the power of the Divine Trinity three times to raise the dead to life.

responsory.text: Martin confessed the faith of the Holy Trinity.
So that he prevailed gloriously in the power of the Divine Trinity three times to raise the dead to life.

verses.text: Si quis autem dómui suæ præésse nescit, quómodo Ecclésiæ Dei diligéntiam habébit?
Non neóphytum, ne in supérbiam elátus, in judícium íncidat diáboli.
Opórtet autem illum et testimónium habére bonum ab iis qui foris sunt, ut non in oppróbrium íncidat, et in láqueum diáboli.

responsory.text: Dómine, si adhuc pópulo tuo sum necessárius, non recúso subíre propter eos labórem:
responsory.repeat: Fiat volúntas tua.

responsory.text: Oculis ac mánibus in cælum semper inténtus, invíctum ab oratióne spíritum non relaxábat.
Fiat volúntas tua.

verses.text: But if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?
Not a neophyte: lest being puffed up with pride, he fall into the judgment of the devil.
Moreover he must have a good testimony of them who are without: lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.

responsory.text: Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work for them.
responsory.repeat: Thy will be done.

responsory.text: With eyes and hands lifted up to heaven, he never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer.
Thy will be done.

verses.text: Exémplum esto fidélium in verbo, in conversatióne, in charitáte, in fide, in castitáte.
Dum vénio, atténde lectióni, exhortatióni, et doctrínæ.
Noli neglígere grátiam, quæ in te est, quæ data est tibi per prophetíam, cum impositióne mánuum presbytérii.
Hæc meditáre, in his esto: ut proféctus tuus maniféstus sit ómnibus.
Atténde tibi, et doctrínæ: insta in illis. Hoc enim fáciens, et teípsum salvum fácies, et eos qui te áudiunt.

responsory.text: O beátum virum Martínum antístitem,
responsory.repeat: Qui nec mori tímuit, nec vívere recusávit!

responsory.text: Dómine, si adhuc pópulo tuo sum necessárius, non recúso labórem: fiat volúntas tua.
Qui nec mori tímuit, nec vívere recusávit!

verses.text: Exémplum esto fidélium in verbo, in conversatióne, in charitáte, in fide, in castitáte.
Dum vénio, atténde lectióni, exhortatióni, et doctrínæ.
Noli neglígere grátiam, quæ in te est, quæ data est tibi per prophetíam, cum impositióne mánuum presbytérii.
Hæc meditáre, in his esto: ut proféctus tuus maniféstus sit ómnibus.
Atténde tibi, et doctrínæ: insta in illis. Hoc enim fáciens, et teípsum salvum fácies, et eos qui te áudiunt.

responsory.text: Oh, how blessed a man was Bishop Martin!
responsory.repeat: He neither feared to die, nor refused to live.

responsory.text: Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work for them. thy will be done.
He neither feared to die, nor refused to live.

verses.text: Præcípio tibi coram Deo, qui vivíficat ómnia, et Christo Jesu, qui testimónium réddidit sub Póntio Piláto, bonam confessiónem,
Ut serves mandátum sine mácula, irreprehensíbile usque in advéntum Dómini nostri Jesu Christi,
Quem suis tempóribus osténdet beátus et solus potens, Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium:
Qui solus habet immortalitátem, et lucem inhábitat inaccessíbilem: quem nullus hóminum vidit, sed nec vidére potest: cui honor, et impérium sempitérnum. Amen.

responsory.text: Dum sacraménta offérret beatus Martínus,
responsory.repeat: Globus ígneus appáruit super caput ejus.

responsory.text: Sum enim ad Deum preces emítteret, † et pro univérso grege sibi commísso deprecarétur.
Globus ígneus appáruit super caput ejus.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Globus ígneus appáruit super caput ejus.

verses.text: Præcípio tibi coram Deo, qui vivíficat ómnia, et Christo Jesu, qui testimónium réddidit sub Póntio Piláto, bonam confessiónem,
Ut serves mandátum sine mácula, irreprehensíbile usque in advéntum Dómini nostri Jesu Christi,
Quem suis tempóribus osténdet beátus et solus potens, Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium:
Qui solus habet immortalitátem, et lucem inhábitat inaccessíbilem: quem nullus hóminum vidit, sed nec vidére potest: cui honor, et impérium sempitérnum. Amen.

responsory.text: When St Martin was offering the sacrament,
responsory.repeat: a ball of fire appeared around his head.

responsory.text: For he sent up his prayers to God imploring him for the who flock that had been entrusted to his care.
A ball of fire appeared around his head.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
A ball of fire appeared around his head.

paragraphs: Martínus, Sabáriæ in Pannónia natus, cum décimum attigísset annum, invítis paréntibus ad ecclésiam confúgiens, in catechumenórum númerum adscríbi vóluit. Quíndecim annos natus in milítiam proféctus, primum in Constántii, deínde Juliáni exércitu militávit. Qui, cum nihil habéret præter arma et vestiméntum quo tegebátur, Ambiáni, páuperi ac nudo, ab eo peténti ut Christi nómine sibi eleemósynam tribúeret, partem chlámydis dedit. Cui sequénti nocte Christus, dimidiáta illa veste indútus, appáruit, hanc mittens vocem: Martínus catechúmenus hac me veste contéxit.

responsory.text: Oculis ac mánibus in cælum semper inténtus,
responsory.repeat: Invíctum ab oratióne spíritum non relaxábat.

responsory.text: Dum sacraménta offérret beátus Martínus, globus ígneus appáruit super caput ejus.
Invíctum ab oratióne spíritum non relaxábat.

paragraphs: Martin was born at Sabaria in Pannonia. When he was ten years old he went to the Church, in the spite of his (heathen) father and mother, and by his own will was numbered among the Catechumens. At fifteen years of age he joined the army, and served as a soldier first under Constantius and then under Julian. Once at the gate of Amiens a poor man asked him for an alms for Christ's name's sake, and since he had nothing to his hand but his arms and his clothes, he gave him half of his cloak. In the night following Christ appeared to him clad in the half of his cloak, and saying (to the angels who bare Him company) While Martin is yet a Catechumen, he hath clad Me in this garment.

responsory.text: With eyes and hands lifted up to heaven
responsory.repeat: He never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer.

responsory.text: While as blessed Martin was offering up the mysteries, a ball of fire appeared above his head.
He never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer.

paragraphs: Decem et octo annos cum habéret, baptizátus est. Quare, relícta militári vita, ad Hilárium Pictaviénsem epíscopum se cóntulit, a quo in acolythórum númerum redáctus est. Post, factus epíscopus Turonénsis, monastérium ædificávit, ubi cum octogínta mónachis sanctíssime aliquámdiu vixit.

responsory.text: Beátus Martínus óbitum suum longe ante præscívit, dixítque frátribus,
responsory.repeat: Dissolutiónem sui córporis imminére, quia judicábat se jam resólvi.

responsory.text: Víribus córporis cœpit repénte destítui, convocatísque discípulis dixit.
Dissolutiónem sui córporis imminére, quia judicábat se jam resólvi.

paragraphs: At eighteen years of age he was baptized. He gave up thereupon the life of a soldier, and betook himself to Hilary, Bishop of Poietiers, by whom he was placed in the order of Acolytes. Being afterwards made Bishop of Tours, he built a monastery wherein he lived in holiness for a while in company of four-score monks.

responsory.text: Blessed Martin knew of his own death of a long time before it came to pass, and he said unto the brethren:
responsory.repeat: That the dissolution of his body was nigh at hand, for he deemed himself to be already breaking up.

responsory.text: His bodily strength gave way all of a sudden, and he called his disciples together, and said unto them
That the dissolution of his body was nigh at hand, for he deemed himself to be already breaking up.

paragraphs: Qui, cum póstea ad Candacénsem vicum suæ diœcésis in gravem febrim incidísset, assídua Deum oratióne precabátur, ut se ex illo mortáli cárcere liberáret. Quem audiéntes discípuli, sic rogábant: Cur nos, pater déseris? cui nos míseros derelínquis? Quorum voce commótus Martínus, ita Deum orábat: Dómine, si adhuc pópulo tuo sum necessárius, non recúso labórem.

responsory.text: Dixérunt discípuli ad beátum Martínum: Cur nos, pater, déseris, aut cui nos desolátos relínquis?
responsory.repeat: Invádent enim gregem tuum lupi rapáces.

responsory.text: Scimus quidem desideráre te Christum, sed salva sunt tibi tua prǽmia: nostri pótius miserére, quos déseris.
Invádent enim gregem tuum lupi rapáces.

paragraphs: At the last he fell sick of a grievous fever at Cande, a village in his diocese, and besought God in constant prayer to set him free from the prison of this dying body. His disciples heard him and said Father, why wilt thou go away from us? unto whom wilt thou bequeath us in our sorrow? Their words moved Martin, and he said Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work.

responsory.text: His disciples said unto blessed Martin: Father, why wilt thou go away from us, and with whom wilt thou leave us orphans?
responsory.repeat: For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.

responsory.text: We know that thou wouldest fain be with Christ, but, sooner or later, thy reward is sure. Rather, then, have pity upon us, whom thou art leaving.
For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.

paragraphs: Sed, cum eum in illa veheménti febre supínum orántem vidérent discípuli, supplíciter ab eo petiérunt, ut, convérso córpore, tantísper, dum remítteret morbi vis, pronus conquiésceret. Quibus Martínus, Sínite me, inquit, cælum pótius quam terram aspícere, ut, suo jam itínere itúrus ad Dóminum, spíritus dirigátur. Instánte jam morte, viso humáni géneris hoste, Quid, inquit, astas, cruénta béstia? nihil in me funéste repéries. Ea in voce, unum et octogínta annos natus, ánimam Deo réddidit; quam Angelórum chorus excépit, eósque divínas canéntes laudes multi, in primísque sanctus Severínus Coloniénsis epíscopus, audiérunt.

responsory.text: O virum ineffábilem, nec labóre victum nec morte vincéndum,
responsory.repeat: Qui nec mori tímuit nec vívere recusávit!

responsory.text: O vere beátum in cujus ore dolus non fuit, † numquam in illíus lingua, nisi Christus, nisi pax, nisi misercórdia ínerat.
Qui nec mori tímuit nec vívere recusávit!
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Qui nec mori tímuit nec vívere recusávit!

paragraphs: When his disciples saw him, in the height of the fever, lying upon his back and praying, they entreated him to turn over and take a little rest upon his side while the violence of his sickness would allow him. But Martin answered them Suffer me to look heavenward rather than earthward, that my spirit may see the way whereby it is so soon going to the Lord. At the moment of death he saw the enemy of mankind, and cried out: What are you come here for, you bloody brute? You murderer, you'll find nothing in me. With these words on his lips, he gave up his soul to God, being aged eighty years. He was received by a company of Angels, who were heard praising God by many persons, especially by holy Severinus, Bishop of Cologne.

responsory.text: O wondrous man not overcome by the work nor vanquished by death
responsory.repeat: Who neither feared death nor was reluctant to live.

responsory.text: O truly blessed in whose mouth there was no deceit, nothing was on his tongue except Christ, except peace, except mercy.
Who neither feared death nor was reluctant to live.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
Who neither feared death nor was reluctant to live.

parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Lucam
paragraphs: In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Nemo lucérnam accéndit et in abscóndito ponit neque sub módio, sed supra candelábrum, ut qui ingrediúntur, lumen vídeant. Et réliqua.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi
parts.source: Liber 7 Comment. in Luc. cap. 11, post initium
paragraphs: Quia in superióribus Ecclésiam Synagógæ prǽtulit, hortátur nos ut fidem pótius nostram ad Ecclésiam transferámus. Lucérna enim fides est, juxta quod scriptum est: Lucérna pédibus meis verbum tuum, Dómine. Verbum enim Dei fides nostra est; Verbum Dei lux est; Lucérna est fides: Erat Lux vera, quæ illúminat omnem hóminem veniéntem in hunc mundum. Lucérna autem lucére non potest, nisi aliúnde lumen accéperit.

responsory.text: O beátum virum, in cujus tránsitu Sanctórum canit númerus, Angelórum exsúltat chorus,
responsory.repeat: Omniúmque cæléstium Virtútum occúrrit psalléntium exércitus!

responsory.text: Ecclésia virtúte roborátur, sacerdótes Dei revelatióne glorificántur, quem Michaël assúmpsit cum Ángelis.
Omniúmque cæléstium Virtútum occúrrit psalléntium exércitus!

parts.title: From the Holy Gospel according to Luke
paragraphs: In that time: Jesus said to his disciples: No man lighteth a candle, and putteth it in a hidden place, nor under a bushel; but upon a candlestick, that they that come in, may see the light. And so on.

parts.title: Homily by St. Ambrose, Bishop (of Milan.)
parts.source: Bk. vii. Comment, on Luke xi.
paragraphs: In that which goeth before, Christ hath set the Church before the synagogue, and He exhorteth us rather to trust in the Church. The candle is faith, even as it is written thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path. (Ps. cxviii. 105.) Our faith is the word of God. The word of God is light. Faith is the candle. It is written concerning the Word of God, that That was the true Light, Which lighteth every man that cometh into this world. (John i. 9.) But a candle cannot shine, unless it be lighted from some other fire.

responsory.text: Blessed indeed was this man, at the time of whose passing the Saints sang in company, a band of Angels shouted aloud for joy
responsory.repeat: And an army of all the Powers of heaven came out to meet him, singing praises.

responsory.text: His strength is a stay to the Church, his manifestation a glory to the Priests of God; Michael and his Angels took him away.
And an army of all the Powers of heaven came out to meet him, singing praises.

paragraphs: Hæc est Lucérna quæ accénditur, virtus scílicet nostræ mentis et sensus, ut drachma illa possit, quæ períerat, reperíri. Nemo ergo fidem sub lege constítuat; lex enim intra mensúram est, ultra mensúram grátia; lex obúmbrat, grátia claríficat. Et ídeo nemo fidem suam intra mensúram legis inclúdat, sed ad Ecclésiam cónferat, in qua septifórmis Spíritus relúcet grátia, quam Princeps ille sacerdótum fulgóre supérnæ divinitátis illúminat, ne eam legis umbra restínguat.

responsory.text: Martínus Ábrahæ sinu lætus excípitur: Martínus, hic pauper et módicus,
responsory.repeat: Cælum dives ingréditur, hymnis cæléstibus honorátur.

responsory.text: Martínus epíscopus migrávit a sǽculo: vivit in Christo gemma sacerdótum.
Cælum dives ingréditur, hymnis cæléstibus honorátur.

paragraphs: Also it is written What woman, having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it? (Luke xv. 8.) And here the candle lighted to find the lost piece is the strength in our understandings and affections. Let no man therefore seek faith under the law. For the law is by measure, but grace without measure; the law overshadoweth, but grace enlighteneth. And therefore let no man shut up his faith within the measure of the law, but give it unto the Church, the Church, wherein shineth the sevenfold grace of the Spirit, and whereon the Divine glory of the Great High Priest doth strike from heaven, lest the shadow of the law should rest any more at all upon her.

responsory.text: Martin was carried joyfully into Abraham's bosom. Martin, who was poor here and of small estimation,
responsory.repeat: Etereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.

responsory.text: Bishop Martin, that jewel of Priests, goeth away from time, liveth in Christ.
Entereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.

paragraphs: Dénique lucérna illa, quam matutínis vespertinísque tempóribus, ritu véteri Judæórum, princeps sacerdótum solébat accéndere, velut sub módio sita legis, evánuit; et cívitas illa Jerúsalem quæ in terris est, quæ occídit prophétas, quasi in conválle fletus pósita delitéscit.

responsory.text: Martínus sacérdos Dei cui post Apóstolos tantam grátiam Dóminus cóntulit, † ut tres mórtuos suscitáret, et álias virtútes præcláras osténderet, inter álios Confessóres et Mártyres
responsory.repeat: Et rosa fulget in Gállia.

responsory.text: Córpore quidem virgíneo blandum habébat elóquium gravis erat in móribus inténta mente cælo suspénsus.
Et rosa fulget in Gállia.

paragraphs: Under the old law there was the sevenfold lamp which the Priest of the Jews lighted every morning and every evening, and this was as it were a candle put under a bushel. That Jerusalem which is upon earth, that Jerusalem which killed the Prophets, lieth hid, as it were, in a dark place in the valley of tears.

responsory.text: Martin, priest of God, who following after the apostles, the Lord united such grace in that he revived three people from death and showed other virtues brilliantly, placing him among the other martyrs and confessors
responsory.repeat: And a rose shone in Gaul

responsory.text: Indeed though his virgin body he was persuasive in his words, his manner was gracious, his mind stretched forth, raised to heaven
And a rose shone in Gaul

paragraphs: Illa autem Jerúsalem quæ in cælo est, in qua mílitat fides nostra, in illo altíssimo ómnium locáta monte, hoc est Christo, non potest ténebris et ruínis hujus mundi abscóndi; sed fulgens candóre Solis ætérni, luce nos grátiæ spiritális illúminat.

responsory.text: Sint lumbi vestri præcíncti, et lucérnæ ardéntes in mánibus vestris:
responsory.repeat: Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.

responsory.text: Vigiláte ergo, quia nescítis qua hora Dóminus vester ventúrus sit.
Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.

paragraphs: But that Jerusalem which is in heaven, whereof by faith we are soldiers, is a city set upon the highest of all mountains, even upon Christ. Her the darkness and tempests of earth cannot hide, but she blazeth with the glory of the Eternal Sun, and maketh to fall upon us the light of spiritual grace.

responsory.text: Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;
responsory.repeat: And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

responsory.text: Watch therefore, for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.
And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

email.preheader: A faithful saying: if a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.
email.html:
A faithful saying: if a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.

Matins · Wednesday, 11 November 2026

St. Martin, Bishop of Tours, Confessor

S. Martini Episcopi et Confessoris · Duplex majus

Commemoration: S. Menna, Martyr

Read in Latin and English

Lesson I

Lesson from the first letter of St. Paul the Apostle to Timothy

1 Tim 3:1-4

A faithful saying: if a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work. It behoveth therefore a bishop to be blameless, the husband of one wife, sober, prudent, of good behaviour, chaste, given to hospitality, a teacher, Not given to wine, no striker, but modest, not quarrelsome, not covetous, but One that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all chastity.

℟. This is that Martin whom God chose to be an High Priest unto Himself, he upon whom the Lord was pleased to bestow favour like as upon His Apostles; * So that he prevailed gloriously in the power of the Divine Trinity three times to raise the dead to life.

℣. Martin confessed the faith of the Holy Trinity.

℟. So that he prevailed gloriously in the power of the Divine Trinity three times to raise the dead to life.

Lesson II

1 Tim 3:5-9

But if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God? Not a neophyte: lest being puffed up with pride, he fall into the judgment of the devil. Moreover he must have a good testimony of them who are without: lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.

℟. Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work for them. * Thy will be done.

℣. With eyes and hands lifted up to heaven, he never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer.

℟. Thy will be done.

Lesson III

1 Tim 4:12-16

Exémplum esto fidélium in verbo, in conversatióne, in charitáte, in fide, in castitáte. Dum vénio, atténde lectióni, exhortatióni, et doctrínæ. Noli neglígere grátiam, quæ in te est, quæ data est tibi per prophetíam, cum impositióne mánuum presbytérii. Hæc meditáre, in his esto: ut proféctus tuus maniféstus sit ómnibus. Atténde tibi, et doctrínæ: insta in illis. Hoc enim fáciens, et teípsum salvum fácies, et eos qui te áudiunt.

℟. Oh, how blessed a man was Bishop Martin! * He neither feared to die, nor refused to live.

℣. Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work for them. thy will be done.

℟. He neither feared to die, nor refused to live.

Lesson IV

1 Tim 6:13-16

Præcípio tibi coram Deo, qui vivíficat ómnia, et Christo Jesu, qui testimónium réddidit sub Póntio Piláto, bonam confessiónem, Ut serves mandátum sine mácula, irreprehensíbile usque in advéntum Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, Quem suis tempóribus osténdet beátus et solus potens, Rex regum, et Dóminus dominántium: Qui solus habet immortalitátem, et lucem inhábitat inaccessíbilem: quem nullus hóminum vidit, sed nec vidére potest: cui honor, et impérium sempitérnum. Amen.

℟. When St Martin was offering the sacrament, * a ball of fire appeared around his head.

℣. For he sent up his prayers to God imploring him for the who flock that had been entrusted to his care.

℟. A ball of fire appeared around his head.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. A ball of fire appeared around his head.

Lesson V

Martin was born at Sabaria in Pannonia. When he was ten years old he went to the Church, in the spite of his (heathen) father and mother, and by his own will was numbered among the Catechumens. At fifteen years of age he joined the army, and served as a soldier first under Constantius and then under Julian. Once at the gate of Amiens a poor man asked him for an alms for Christ's name's sake, and since he had nothing to his hand but his arms and his clothes, he gave him half of his cloak. In the night following Christ appeared to him clad in the half of his cloak, and saying (to the angels who bare Him company) While Martin is yet a Catechumen, he hath clad Me in this garment.

℟. With eyes and hands lifted up to heaven * He never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer.

℣. While as blessed Martin was offering up the mysteries, a ball of fire appeared above his head.

℟. He never let his mighty spirit slacken in prayer.

Lesson VI

At eighteen years of age he was baptized. He gave up thereupon the life of a soldier, and betook himself to Hilary, Bishop of Poietiers, by whom he was placed in the order of Acolytes. Being afterwards made Bishop of Tours, he built a monastery wherein he lived in holiness for a while in company of four-score monks.

℟. Blessed Martin knew of his own death of a long time before it came to pass, and he said unto the brethren: * That the dissolution of his body was nigh at hand, for he deemed himself to be already breaking up.

℣. His bodily strength gave way all of a sudden, and he called his disciples together, and said unto them

℟. That the dissolution of his body was nigh at hand, for he deemed himself to be already breaking up.

Lesson VII

At the last he fell sick of a grievous fever at Cande, a village in his diocese, and besought God in constant prayer to set him free from the prison of this dying body. His disciples heard him and said Father, why wilt thou go away from us? unto whom wilt thou bequeath us in our sorrow? Their words moved Martin, and he said Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work.

℟. His disciples said unto blessed Martin: Father, why wilt thou go away from us, and with whom wilt thou leave us orphans? * For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.

℣. We know that thou wouldest fain be with Christ, but, sooner or later, thy reward is sure. Rather, then, have pity upon us, whom thou art leaving.

℟. For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.

Lesson VIII

When his disciples saw him, in the height of the fever, lying upon his back and praying, they entreated him to turn over and take a little rest upon his side while the violence of his sickness would allow him. But Martin answered them Suffer me to look heavenward rather than earthward, that my spirit may see the way whereby it is so soon going to the Lord. At the moment of death he saw the enemy of mankind, and cried out: What are you come here for, you bloody brute? You murderer, you'll find nothing in me. With these words on his lips, he gave up his soul to God, being aged eighty years. He was received by a company of Angels, who were heard praising God by many persons, especially by holy Severinus, Bishop of Cologne.

℟. O wondrous man not overcome by the work nor vanquished by death * Who neither feared death nor was reluctant to live.

℣. O truly blessed in whose mouth there was no deceit, nothing was on his tongue except Christ, except peace, except mercy.

℟. Who neither feared death nor was reluctant to live.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Who neither feared death nor was reluctant to live.

Lesson IX

From the Holy Gospel according to Luke

Luke 11:33-36

In that time: Jesus said to his disciples: No man lighteth a candle, and putteth it in a hidden place, nor under a bushel; but upon a candlestick, that they that come in, may see the light. And so on.

Homily by St. Ambrose, Bishop (of Milan.)

Bk. vii. Comment, on Luke xi.

In that which goeth before, Christ hath set the Church before the synagogue, and He exhorteth us rather to trust in the Church. The candle is faith, even as it is written thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path. (Ps. cxviii. 105.) Our faith is the word of God. The word of God is light. Faith is the candle. It is written concerning the Word of God, that That was the true Light, Which lighteth every man that cometh into this world. (John i. 9.) But a candle cannot shine, unless it be lighted from some other fire.

℟. Blessed indeed was this man, at the time of whose passing the Saints sang in company, a band of Angels shouted aloud for joy * And an army of all the Powers of heaven came out to meet him, singing praises.

℣. His strength is a stay to the Church, his manifestation a glory to the Priests of God; Michael and his Angels took him away.

℟. And an army of all the Powers of heaven came out to meet him, singing praises.

Lesson X

Also it is written What woman, having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it? (Luke xv. 8.) And here the candle lighted to find the lost piece is the strength in our understandings and affections. Let no man therefore seek faith under the law. For the law is by measure, but grace without measure; the law overshadoweth, but grace enlighteneth. And therefore let no man shut up his faith within the measure of the law, but give it unto the Church, the Church, wherein shineth the sevenfold grace of the Spirit, and whereon the Divine glory of the Great High Priest doth strike from heaven, lest the shadow of the law should rest any more at all upon her.

℟. Martin was carried joyfully into Abraham's bosom. Martin, who was poor here and of small estimation, * Etereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.

℣. Bishop Martin, that jewel of Priests, goeth away from time, liveth in Christ.

℟. Entereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.

Lesson XI

Under the old law there was the sevenfold lamp which the Priest of the Jews lighted every morning and every evening, and this was as it were a candle put under a bushel. That Jerusalem which is upon earth, that Jerusalem which killed the Prophets, lieth hid, as it were, in a dark place in the valley of tears.

℟. Martin, priest of God, who following after the apostles, the Lord united such grace in that he revived three people from death and showed other virtues brilliantly, placing him among the other martyrs and confessors * And a rose shone in Gaul

℣. Indeed though his virgin body he was persuasive in his words, his manner was gracious, his mind stretched forth, raised to heaven

℟. And a rose shone in Gaul

Lesson XII

But that Jerusalem which is in heaven, whereof by faith we are soldiers, is a city set upon the highest of all mountains, even upon Christ. Her the darkness and tempests of earth cannot hide, but she blazeth with the glory of the Eternal Sun, and maketh to fall upon us the light of spiritual grace.

℟. Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning; * And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

℣. Watch therefore, for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.

℟. And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

Te Deum

Read in Latin and English

Cistercian Breviary, 1951. Texts from Divinum Officium (divinumofficium.com).

Lesson VI

Decem et octo annos cum habéret, baptizátus est. Quare, relícta militári vita, ad Hilárium Pictaviénsem epíscopum se cóntulit, a quo in acolythórum númerum redáctus est. Post, factus epíscopus Turonénsis, monastérium ædificávit, ubi cum octogínta mónachis sanctíssime aliquámdiu vixit.

Being afterwards made Bishop of Tours, he built a monastery wherein he lived in holiness for a while in company of four-score monks.

℟. Beátus Martínus óbitum suum longe ante præscívit, dixítque frátribus, * Dissolutiónem sui córporis imminére, quia judicábat se jam resólvi.

℟. Blessed Martin knew of his own death of a long time before it came to pass, and he said unto the brethren: * That the dissolution of his body was nigh at hand, for he deemed himself to be already breaking up.

℣. Víribus córporis cœpit repénte destítui, convocatísque discípulis dixit.

℣. His bodily strength gave way all of a sudden, and he called his disciples together, and said unto them

℟. Dissolutiónem sui córporis imminére, quia judicábat se jam resólvi.

℟. That the dissolution of his body was nigh at hand, for he deemed himself to be already breaking up.

Lectio VII

Lesson VII

Qui, cum póstea ad Candacénsem vicum suæ diœcésis in gravem febrim incidísset, assídua Deum oratióne precabátur, ut se ex illo mortáli cárcere liberáret. Quem audiéntes discípuli, sic rogábant: Cur nos, pater déseris? cui nos míseros derelínquis? Quorum voce commótus Martínus, ita Deum orábat: Dómine, si adhuc pópulo tuo sum necessárius, non recúso labórem.

At the last he fell sick of a grievous fever at Cande, a village in his diocese, and besought God in constant prayer to set him free from the prison of this dying body. His disciples heard him and said Father, why wilt thou go away from us? unto whom wilt thou bequeath us in our sorrow? Their words moved Martin, and he said Lord, if I be still needful to thy people, I refuse not to work.

℟. Dixérunt discípuli ad beátum Martínum: Cur nos, pater, déseris, aut cui nos desolátos relínquis? * Invádent enim gregem tuum lupi rapáces.

℟. His disciples said unto blessed Martin: Father, why wilt thou go away from us, and with whom wilt thou leave us orphans? * For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.

℣. Scimus quidem desideráre te Christum, sed salva sunt tibi tua prǽmia: nostri pótius miserére, quos déseris.

℣. We know that thou wouldest fain be with Christ, but, sooner or later, thy reward is sure. Rather, then, have pity upon us, whom thou art leaving.

℟. Invádent enim gregem tuum lupi rapáces.

℟. For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.

Lectio VIII

Lesson VIII

Sed, cum eum in illa veheménti febre supínum orántem vidérent discípuli, supplíciter ab eo petiérunt, ut, convérso córpore, tantísper, dum remítteret morbi vis, pronus conquiésceret. Quibus Martínus, Sínite me, inquit, cælum pótius quam terram aspícere, ut, suo jam itínere itúrus ad Dóminum, spíritus dirigátur. Instánte jam morte, viso humáni géneris hoste, Quid, inquit, astas, cruénta béstia? nihil in me funéste repéries. Ea in voce, unum et octogínta annos natus, ánimam Deo réddidit; quam Angelórum chorus excépit, eósque divínas canéntes laudes multi, in primísque sanctus Severínus Coloniénsis epíscopus, audiérunt.

When his disciples saw him, in the height of the fever, lying upon his back and praying, they entreated him to turn over and take a little rest upon his side while the violence of his sickness would allow him. But Martin answered them Suffer me to look heavenward rather than earthward, that my spirit may see the way whereby it is so soon going to the Lord. At the moment of death he saw the enemy of mankind, and cried out: What are you come here for, you bloody brute? You murderer, you'll find nothing in me. With these words on his lips, he gave up his soul to God, being aged eighty years. He was received by a company of Angels, who were heard praising God by many persons, especially by holy Severinus, Bishop of Cologne.

℟. O virum ineffábilem, nec labóre victum nec morte vincéndum, * Qui nec mori tímuit nec vívere recusávit!

℟. O wondrous man not overcome by the work nor vanquished by death * Who neither feared death nor was reluctant to live.

℣. O vere beátum in cujus ore dolus non fuit, † numquam in illíus lingua, nisi Christus, nisi pax, nisi misercórdia ínerat.

℣. O truly blessed in whose mouth there was no deceit, nothing was on his tongue except Christ, except peace, except mercy.

℟. Qui nec mori tímuit nec vívere recusávit!

℟. Who neither feared death nor was reluctant to live.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Qui nec mori tímuit nec vívere recusávit!

℟. Who neither feared death nor was reluctant to live.

Lectio IX

Lesson IX

Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Lucam

From the Holy Gospel according to Luke

Luc 11:33-36

Luke 11:33-36

In illo témpore: Dixit Jesus discípulis suis: Nemo lucérnam accéndit et in abscóndito ponit neque sub módio, sed supra candelábrum, ut qui ingrediúntur, lumen vídeant. Et réliqua.

In that time: Jesus said to his disciples: No man lighteth a candle, and putteth it in a hidden place, nor under a bushel; but upon a candlestick, that they that come in, may see the light. And so on.

Homilía sancti Ambrósii Epíscopi

Homily by St. Ambrose, Bishop (of Milan.)

Liber 7 Comment. in Luc. cap. 11, post initium

Bk. vii. Comment, on Luke xi.

Quia in superióribus Ecclésiam Synagógæ prǽtulit, hortátur nos ut fidem pótius nostram ad Ecclésiam transferámus. Lucérna enim fides est, juxta quod scriptum est: Lucérna pédibus meis verbum tuum, Dómine. Verbum enim Dei fides nostra est; Verbum Dei lux est; Lucérna est fides: Erat Lux vera, quæ illúminat omnem hóminem veniéntem in hunc mundum. Lucérna autem lucére non potest, nisi aliúnde lumen accéperit.

In that which goeth before, Christ hath set the Church before the synagogue, and He exhorteth us rather to trust in the Church. The candle is faith, even as it is written thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path. (Ps. cxviii. 105.) Our faith is the word of God. The word of God is light. Faith is the candle. It is written concerning the Word of God, that That was the true Light, Which lighteth every man that cometh into this world. (John i. 9.) But a candle cannot shine, unless it be lighted from some other fire.

℟. O beátum virum, in cujus tránsitu Sanctórum canit númerus, Angelórum exsúltat chorus, * Omniúmque cæléstium Virtútum occúrrit psalléntium exércitus!

℟. Blessed indeed was this man, at the time of whose passing the Saints sang in company, a band of Angels shouted aloud for joy * And an army of all the Powers of heaven came out to meet him, singing praises.

℣. Ecclésia virtúte roborátur, sacerdótes Dei revelatióne glorificántur, quem Michaël assúmpsit cum Ángelis.

℣. His strength is a stay to the Church, his manifestation a glory to the Priests of God; Michael and his Angels took him away.

℟. Omniúmque cæléstium Virtútum occúrrit psalléntium exércitus!

℟. And an army of all the Powers of heaven came out to meet him, singing praises.

Lectio X

Lesson X

Hæc est Lucérna quæ accénditur, virtus scílicet nostræ mentis et sensus, ut drachma illa possit, quæ períerat, reperíri. Nemo ergo fidem sub lege constítuat; lex enim intra mensúram est, ultra mensúram grátia; lex obúmbrat, grátia claríficat. Et ídeo nemo fidem suam intra mensúram legis inclúdat, sed ad Ecclésiam cónferat, in qua septifórmis Spíritus relúcet grátia, quam Princeps ille sacerdótum fulgóre supérnæ divinitátis illúminat, ne eam legis umbra restínguat.

Also it is written What woman, having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it? (Luke xv. 8.) And here the candle lighted to find the lost piece is the strength in our understandings and affections. Let no man therefore seek faith under the law. For the law is by measure, but grace without measure; the law overshadoweth, but grace enlighteneth. And therefore let no man shut up his faith within the measure of the law, but give it unto the Church, the Church, wherein shineth the sevenfold grace of the Spirit, and whereon the Divine glory of the Great High Priest doth strike from heaven, lest the shadow of the law should rest any more at all upon her.

℟. Martínus Ábrahæ sinu lætus excípitur: Martínus, hic pauper et módicus, * Cælum dives ingréditur, hymnis cæléstibus honorátur.

℟. Martin was carried joyfully into Abraham's bosom. Martin, who was poor here and of small estimation, * Etereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.

℣. Martínus epíscopus migrávit a sǽculo: vivit in Christo gemma sacerdótum.

℣. Bishop Martin, that jewel of Priests, goeth away from time, liveth in Christ.

℟. Cælum dives ingréditur, hymnis cæléstibus honorátur.

℟. Entereth rich into heaven, and the songs of heaven are raised in his honour.

Lectio XI

Lesson XI

Dénique lucérna illa, quam matutínis vespertinísque tempóribus, ritu véteri Judæórum, princeps sacerdótum solébat accéndere, velut sub módio sita legis, evánuit; et cívitas illa Jerúsalem quæ in terris est, quæ occídit prophétas, quasi in conválle fletus pósita delitéscit.

Under the old law there was the sevenfold lamp which the Priest of the Jews lighted every morning and every evening, and this was as it were a candle put under a bushel. That Jerusalem which is upon earth, that Jerusalem which killed the Prophets, lieth hid, as it were, in a dark place in the valley of tears.

℟. Martínus sacérdos Dei cui post Apóstolos tantam grátiam Dóminus cóntulit, † ut tres mórtuos suscitáret, et álias virtútes præcláras osténderet, inter álios Confessóres et Mártyres * Et rosa fulget in Gállia.

℟. Martin, priest of God, who following after the apostles, the Lord united such grace in that he revived three people from death and showed other virtues brilliantly, placing him among the other martyrs and confessors * And a rose shone in Gaul

℣. Córpore quidem virgíneo blandum habébat elóquium gravis erat in móribus inténta mente cælo suspénsus.

℣. Indeed though his virgin body he was persuasive in his words, his manner was gracious, his mind stretched forth, raised to heaven

℟. Et rosa fulget in Gállia.

℟. And a rose shone in Gaul

Lectio XII

Lesson XII

Illa autem Jerúsalem quæ in cælo est, in qua mílitat fides nostra, in illo altíssimo ómnium locáta monte, hoc est Christo, non potest ténebris et ruínis hujus mundi abscóndi; sed fulgens candóre Solis ætérni, luce nos grátiæ spiritális illúminat.

But that Jerusalem which is in heaven, whereof by faith we are soldiers, is a city set upon the highest of all mountains, even upon Christ. Her the darkness and tempests of earth cannot hide, but she blazeth with the glory of the Eternal Sun, and maketh to fall upon us the light of spiritual grace.

℟. Sint lumbi vestri præcíncti, et lucérnæ ardéntes in mánibus vestris: * Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.

℟. Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning; * And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

℣. Vigiláte ergo, quia nescítis qua hora Dóminus vester ventúrus sit.

℣. Watch therefore, for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.

℟. Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.

℟. And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Et vos símiles homínibus exspectántibus dóminum suum, quando revertátur a núptiis.

℟. And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding.
